title: ReadinessProfile
description: Tracewell's position across the five readiness categories of Jöhnk et al. (2021) and on the OECD/WEF maturity view. The whole profile describes a fictional team and is labelled fictional; the framework citation is real and labelled so. There is no numeric field anywhere: a category holds answers and a prose finding, never a score, bar value or level of strength (A-10). The maturity level is held as a name only, with no level number, and is pinned to the literal LEVEL_NAME_UNVERIFIED until the report is verified (D-1). The next complement is pinned to null until K-2 is decided. Shipped in data/readiness.js.

subject.description: The fictional team the profile describes (Tracewell).

categories.description: Exactly five categories, each key exactly once, in the order the paper presents them. Here, unlike elsewhere, array order is meaningful: it is the source's order, not an order of importance, and the UI never re-sorts it by finding.

key.description: Machine key. The five keys follow the category names as L2 records them from the paper; the Verifier confirms the names before freeze (Decision DM-8).

name.description: The category name exactly as confirmed against the paper, for display.

answers.description: Tracewell's answers from the persona dossier, as question and answer pairs, in dossier order.

finding.description: Prose only: what the answers show about this category. No level, grade or strength word is carried in a separate field, and C-6 applies to the prose.

status.description: Whether the level names and criteria have been confirmed by Miguel against the OECD/WEF report itself.

nextComplement.description: Pinned to null until K-2 decides whether a single next complement is compatible with the no-recommendation invariant, and in what form. The shape is re-specified then.
